page.notes: The long s is written as plain s throughout (e.g. "falsum", "necessitate", "suaviter"). The f-shaped letters in the scan are long s, not f. "Jesuita" is printed with a capital I that reads as a consonant; written as J per the i/j rule. Line 22 "agere,ut" is printed without a space; kept as printed. "obstracte" (line 25): the first letters are unclear; read as "obstracte" with [?]. The last word "tiva" (applicativa) is set alone under the final line, so it is recorded as the catchword and the text ends at "applica-". Stray marks at the left and right edges of the scan are not printed text and are left out.
